before.title: Cold-Start Delay or No-Start After Overnight Parking (Excessive Cold-Start Fuel Injection — ECU Service Campaign)
before.description: Early TA Morning vehicles built between January 15, 2011 and March 28, 2012 suffer intermittent hard starting after a long cold soak (typically winter mornings): the engine cranks, almost catches, then dies or refuses to start. Kia identified the cause as excessive fuel-injection quantity at cold start producing unstable combustion, and issued a free-repair campaign (무상수리) consisting of an ECU software upgrade. Korean owner forums also document residual cold-start delay on later TA cars (e.g., 2015 models) that was ultimately resolved by replacing the fuel pump assembly when the ECU update alone did not cure it.
before.solution: Have a Kia service center apply the cold-start ECU calibration update (free under the campaign for cars built Jan 2011-Mar 2012). If delayed cold starts persist after the update, test fuel-rail pressure hold-down; a leaking check valve in the in-tank fuel pump assembly is the documented follow-up fix. Rule out a weak battery first in sub-zero weather.
symptoms: Long cranking on cold mornings after overnight parking
Engine almost starts then dies, needs several attempts
Problem appears mainly in winter or after long cold soak
Rough running for the first seconds after a cold start
Starts normally once the engine is warm

before.title: Crankshaft Rear Main Seal (Retainer) Oil Leak Between Engine and Transmission
before.description: A widely reported chronic problem on the TA Morning: the crankshaft rear oil seal (크랭크 리데나/리테이너) loses tension or walks out of position, letting engine oil leak at the junction between the engine and transmission. Korean repair shops document this as a recurring Morning failure, and owner communities report that Kia quietly issued a one-time free-repair directive to its Auto Q service network for this leak, though application was inconsistent between service centers. Because the seal sits behind the transmission, the gearbox must be removed to replace a cheap part, making the repair disproportionately expensive — roughly 300,000-350,000 KRW out of pocket. On manual cars, leaking oil can contaminate the clutch and cause slip.
before.solution: Replace the crankshaft rear oil seal/retainer; transmission removal is required, so combine with clutch service on manual cars if the clutch is oil-contaminated. Ask a Kia Auto Q service center whether the one-time free repair (무상수리) for the crank retainer leak applies to the vehicle before paying out of pocket — coverage reports vary by center.
symptoms: Oil drips or wetness where engine meets transmission
Oil spots under the middle of the car
Engine oil level slowly dropping
Burning oil smell after driving
Clutch slip or shudder on manual cars (oil-contaminated clutch)

before.title: Drive-Belt 'Cricket' Squeal from Solid Alternator Pulley (Early Kappa 1.0)
before.description: 2011 to late-2012 production Morning (TA) and Ray cars with the early 1.0 Kappa engine are notorious in Korea for a chirping/squealing 'cricket noise' (귀뚜라미 소리) from the accessory belt, worst on cold mornings and when the A/C compressor engages. The root cause is the solid (fixed) alternator pulley, which cannot absorb rapid crankshaft speed fluctuations of the 3-cylinder engine, so the belt repeatedly slips. Kia revised production from the 2013 model year, fitting an OAP (overrunning alternator pulley) and changing the belt from 5 to 6 ribs; replacing the solid pulley with the OAP type is the accepted permanent fix. Simply replacing the belt does not cure it — the noise returns.
before.solution: Replace the solid alternator pulley with the revised OAP (overrunning alternator pulley) and fit the updated 6-rib drive belt per the 2013 production change. Belt dressing or belt replacement alone gives only temporary relief. Parts plus labor typically run 150,000-300,000 KRW at independent shops in Korea.
symptoms: Chirping/squealing 'cricket' noise at cold start
Noise appears when the A/C is switched on
Worse in winter or damp weather
Noise returns soon after a new belt is fitted
Noise varies with engine RPM

before.title: Fuel and Leveling Hose Cracking — Fuel Leak and Fire Risk (Official Korean Recall)
before.description: In April 2018, Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) recalled 190,562 Kia Morning (TA) and Ray (TAM) vehicles because the fuel hose and fuel-tank leveling hose were made from a defective material that cracks over time. Cracked hoses allow fuel (gasoline or LPG vapor on Bi-Fuel models) to leak, creating a fire hazard. The recall population corresponds to early TA-generation production; affected VINs can be checked on Korea's official recall portal (car.go.kr). This recall applies to the Korea-market Morning; the related Picanto sold in other markets had separate campaigns.
before.solution: Covered free of charge under the official recall: Kia service centers inspect the fuel and leveling hoses and replace them with hoses made of corrected material. Owners who paid for this repair before the recall announcement could claim reimbursement from Kia. Check recall applicability by VIN at car.go.kr; if a fuel smell or visible leak is present, stop driving and have the car towed to a service center.
symptoms: Gasoline smell inside or around the car
Fuel stains or wet spots under the rear of the vehicle
Visible cracking on fuel hoses
Dropping fuel level without corresponding mileage
Fuel-vapor smell when refueling (Bi-Fuel/LPI cars)

before.title: Manual Transmission Clutch Judder and Rapid Clutch/Flywheel Wear
before.description: Manual-gearbox Morning/Picanto cars show two related, well-documented clutch complaints. First, cold/damp-morning clutch judder: a pronounced shudder when pulling away in 1st or 2nd gear that fades after a few miles, attributed to condensation on the friction surfaces and addressed by revised clutch part numbers — repeatedly discussed across Kia Owners Club threads for the Picanto (the Morning's twin, same platform and drivetrain family). Second, Korean owner communities document low durability of the clutch and flywheel on the TA Morning: habitual half-clutch driving can glaze or burn the friction plate in remarkably low mileage, and uneven flywheel wear then perpetuates judder even after a new clutch. Korea-market evidence is the Morning TA; the judder threads are from the EU-market Picanto with shared running gear.
before.solution: For persistent judder, replace the clutch kit (disc, pressure plate, release bearing) with the latest revised parts and resurface or replace the flywheel — fitting a new clutch against a worn flywheel commonly brings the judder back. Under warranty, dealers handled judder cases with updated clutch components. Adjust driving habits to minimize riding the clutch; on cars that only judder damp-cold and clear within a mile, monitor before paying for repairs.
symptoms: Shudder/vibration when pulling away, worst on cold or damp mornings
Judder fades after a few minutes of driving
Clutch slip — revs rise without acceleration
Burning smell after hill starts or stop-and-go traffic
High or inconsistent clutch bite point at low mileage

before.title: PCV Valve Plastic Needle Wear — Oil Ingestion and White Exhaust Smoke (Government-Ordered Recall)
before.description: On the 1.0L Kappa engine in Morning and Ray vehicles built between January 17, 2011 and July 16, 2012 (196,950 vehicles total), the PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve used a plastic needle with poor durability. As the needle wears, the valve no longer regulates blow-by gas correctly and engine oil is drawn into the intake manifold, where it burns with fuel and produces white exhaust smoke with elevated particulate emissions. Korea's Ministry of Environment ordered a corrective recall in March 2014, replacing the plastic valve with a steel one. Beyond the smoke, unaddressed valves cause gradual engine-oil consumption and intake fouling.
before.solution: Free replacement of the plastic PCV valve with a steel-needle PCV valve at Kia service centers under the March 2014 campaign. Outside the campaign, replacing the PCV valve is an inexpensive repair; also check and top up engine oil, and clean the intake/throttle body if heavy oil ingestion has occurred. Owners of 2011-2012 cars showing white smoke should confirm the steel valve was fitted.
symptoms: White smoke from the exhaust, especially under acceleration
Engine oil level drops between services
Burning-oil smell
Oily residue in the intake/throttle body
Rough idle

proposal.title: PCV Valve Plastic Needle Wear — Oil Ingestion and White Exhaust Smoke (Government-Ordered Recall)
proposal.description: South Korea's Ministry of Environment states that Kia recalled Morning 1.0 gasoline and Morning 1.0 Bi-Fuel vehicles produced from January 17, 2011 through July 16, 2012 because the plastic needle in the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve could wear. The worn valve can allow engine oil into the intake manifold, where it burns with fuel and can produce white exhaust smoke and increased particulate emissions. The cited total of 196,950 vehicles covers four Morning and Ray variants together, not Morning alone.
proposal.solution: Confirm campaign completion with a Kia service center. The government notice says Kia service centers and partners inspect and replace the PCV valve free of charge, changing the needle material from plastic to steel. This is a Korean-market campaign repair with vehicle-specific applicability, so no retail PCV valve is linked from this page.
symptoms: White exhaust smoke
